\subsection*{Expanders --- Foundations: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.Expanders.Basic}.

\subsection*{Expanders --- Foundations: Results}

\begin{definition}[Symmetric stochastic matrix]
\lean{Expander.IsSymmStochastic}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p038-b004,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p039-b002
}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p021-b002}
\label{Expander.IsSymmStochastic}
\leanok
A real matrix indexed by a finite set of $n$ indices is symmetric, has nonnegative
entries, and each row sums to $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform vector]
\lean{Expander.uniform}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p039-b003,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p040-b001
}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p021-b002,
  pdf-26d95080dbde-p021-b003
}
\label{Expander.uniform}
\leanok
For $n$ coordinates, the uniform vector in Euclidean space is the vector whose every
coordinate equals $1/n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Matrix-induced linear map]
\lean{Expander.toCLM}
\label{Expander.toCLM}
\leanok
For a real matrix $A$ indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let its associated continuous
linear map on $\mathbb R^n$ send a vector $x$ to the vector whose $i$th coordinate is
$\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} A_{ij}x_j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinates of the uniform vector]
\lean{Expander.uniform_apply}
\label{Expander.uniform_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.uniform}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$ and every index $i\in\text{Fin}(n)$, the $i$th coordinate
of the uniform vector in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $1/n$, interpreted as the real reciprocal of
$n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate formula for a matrix operator]
\lean{Expander.toCLM_apply_coord}
\label{Expander.toCLM_apply_coord}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.toCLM}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ be a real matrix indexed by $	ext{Fin}(n)$ and let $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$ with the
Euclidean norm. For each index $i$, the $i$th coordinate of the operator associated with
$A$ applied to $v$ is $\sum_j A_{ij}v_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Euclidean Inner Product Formula]
\lean{Expander.inner_eq_sum}
\label{Expander.inner_eq_sum}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and vectors $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n$, their Euclidean
inner product is $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetry of the Matrix Operator]
\lean{Expander.inner_toCLM_right}
\label{Expander.inner_toCLM_right}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.inner_eq_sum, Expander.toCLM, Expander.toCLM_apply_coord}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $A$ be a symmetric real $n\times n$ matrix. For
all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n$, one has $\langle Ax,y\rangle=\langle x,Ay\rangle$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Norm of the Uniform Vector]
\lean{Expander.inner_uniform_self}
\label{Expander.inner_uniform_self}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.inner_eq_sum, Expander.uniform}
\difficulty{4}
For every nonnegative integer $n$, let $u\in\mathbb{R}^n$ be the constant vector whose
coordinates are $1/n$. Then $\langle u,u\rangle=1/n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Homogeneity of matrix operators]
\lean{Expander.toCLM_smul}
\label{Expander.toCLM_smul}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.toCLM}
\difficulty{3}
For every real scalar $c$ and real matrix $A$ indexed by $	ext{Fin}(n)$, the operator
associated with $cA$ is $c$ times the operator associated with $A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity of matrix operators]
\lean{Expander.toCLM_add}
\label{Expander.toCLM_add}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.toCLM}
\difficulty{3}
For real matrices $A$ and $B$ indexed by $	ext{Fin}(n)$, the continuous linear operator
associated with their sum is the sum of the continuous linear operators associated with
$A$ and $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subtraction of matrix operators]
\lean{Expander.toCLM_sub}
\label{Expander.toCLM_sub}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.toCLM}
\difficulty{3}
For real matrices $A$ and $B$ indexed by $	ext{Fin}(n)$, the operator associated with
$A-B$ is the operator associated with $A$ minus the operator associated with $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Orthogonal operator norm]
\lean{Expander.lambda}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p040-b001,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p108-b004,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p308-b004,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p309-b001
}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p021-b003}
\label{Expander.lambda}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.toCLM, Expander.uniform}
For a real matrix $A$ on $n$ coordinates, define its value on the subspace orthogonal to
the uniform vector as $\sup\{\|Av\| : \|v\|=1,\ v\perp\mathbf{1}\}$, where $\mathbf{1}$ is the
uniform vector.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform vector is fixed]
\lean{Expander.mulVec_uniform}
\label{Expander.mulVec_uniform}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.toCLM, Expander.uniform}
\difficulty{3}
Let $A$ be a real $n\times n$ matrix that is symmetric, has nonnegative entries, and has
every row sum equal to $1$. Then $A$ fixes the constant vector whose entries are $1/n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Contraction on the orthogonal subspace]
\lean{Expander.norm_mulVec_le_lambda}
\label{Expander.norm_mulVec_le_lambda}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.lambda, Expander.toCLM, Expander.uniform}
\difficulty{5}
Let $A$ be a real $n\times n$ symmetric matrix with nonnegative entries and row sums
equal to $1$, and define $\lambda(A)$ as the supremum of $\|Au\|$ over unit vectors
orthogonal to the constant vector whose entries are $1/n$. For every vector $v$
orthogonal to that constant vector, $\|Av\|\le \lambda(A)\|v\|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of the spectral parameter]
\lean{Expander.lambda_nonneg}
\label{Expander.lambda_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.lambda}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge 2$ and let $A$ be a real $n\times n$ matrix. Define $\lambda(A)$ as the
supremum of $\|Av\|$ over unit vectors $v$ orthogonal to the constant vector whose
entries are $1/n$. Then $\lambda(A)\ge 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Contraction of a symmetric stochastic matrix]
\lean{Expander.norm_toCLM_apply_le}
\label{Expander.norm_toCLM_apply_le}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.toCLM}
\difficulty{5}
Let $A$ be a real $n\times n$ symmetric matrix with nonnegative entries and every row
sum equal to $1$. Then for every vector $v\in\mathbb R^n$, $\|Av\|\le\|v\|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on the Nontrivial Operator Norm]
\lean{Expander.lambda_le_one}
\label{Expander.lambda_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.lambda, Expander.norm_toCLM_apply_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $A$ be a symmetric real $n\times n$ matrix with
nonnegative entries and every row summing to $1$. Let $\lambda(A)$ be the supremum of
$\|Av\|$ over unit vectors $v$ orthogonal to the constant vector with every coordinate
$1/n$. Then $\lambda(A)\leq 1$.
\end{theorem}
